issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an instance method addRating(stars:) on Course (parameter label 'stars'), but the solution's Course implementation defines addRating(rating:) (parameter label 'rating'). Additionally, the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:), which does not match the solution Course method. This parameter-label mismatch is structural and will cause compilation or usage errors and confusion about the correct method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter label consistent across all artifacts. Change the solution Course method signature to addRating(stars: Int) (rename the parameter from 'rating' to 'stars'), or alternatively update the problem statement, template, and client usages to use addRating(rating: Int). Prefer matching the problem/template by using addRating(stars:) so student-facing materials and starter code remain aligned.

issues.description: The parameter name for the course rating is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template use addRating(stars:), but the solution implements addRating(rating:) while the solution's Client calls addRating(stars:). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual parameter (number of stars) creates confusion and can cause compilation or usage errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement and template by changing the solution method signature to `func addRating(stars: Int)` and use `stars` internally (or update the Client calls to the chosen name). Ensure all references (including tests or Client) use the same label.
